result.dimension: argv[3] -> int conversion (std::stoi) and how port() / to_string() render it

rules.rule: argv[3] is converted with std::stoi(argv[3]) using base 10 BEFORE the Url object is built or anything is printed. Accepted grammar (strtol semantics): [ \t\n\v\f\r]* [+|-]? DIGIT+ <anything-ignored>. Leading ASCII whitespace is skipped, one optional sign is allowed, then one or more ASCII '0'-'9' digits are consumed, and parsing STOPS at the first non-digit; all trailing characters are silently ignored.
Base is 10 only: "0x", "0X", "0b" prefixes are NOT recognized. The leading '0' is consumed as a digit and parsing stops at 'x'/'X'/'b', yielding 0.
rules.evidence: "0x50"->port 0, to_string "http://example.com:0/", exit=0; "0X50"->0; "0b11"->0; "0x7fffffff"->0

rules.rule: If, after optional whitespace and an optional sign, there is NO ASCII decimal digit, std::stoi throws std::invalid_argument. The exception is NOT caught: the program calls std::terminate and dies on SIGABRT. Exit status is 134 (128+6, shell reports "Aborted (core dumped)"). stdout is EXACTLY 0 bytes (even with stdbuf -o0, i.e. nothing is printed before the throw). stderr is exactly the 87 bytes: "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument'\n  what():  stoi\n" (note TWO spaces before 'what()' and TWO spaces after the colon).

Negative zero and signed zero normalize to 0 (in range), so port() prints "0" and to_string INCLUDES ":0".

rules.rule:
to_string() is the concatenation of exactly 4 blocks in this fixed order: [authority block] + path + query block + fragment block. Full pseudocode (validated 26/26 against an independent predictor):

  s = ""
  if (scheme != "") {          // scheme here is the already-lowercased stored scheme
      s += scheme + "://"
      s += host                  // verbatim, no case folding, no encoding
      if (port >= 0) s += ":" + decimal(port)   // port is the already-normalized stored port
  }
  s += path                      // the already-normalized stored path (leading '/' added at construction)
  if (query    != "") s += "?" + query
  if (fragment != "") s += "#" + fragment
  return s

No other characters are ever inserted (no userinfo, no '@', no separator between authority and path, no default '/' path).

rules.rule: The ENTIRE authority block ("scheme" + "://" + host + optional ":port") is gated on scheme being non-empty. It is NOT gated on host and NOT gated on port. If scheme == "", then host AND port are both completely absent from to_string() even when they are non-empty/valid.

rules.rule: The separator is an unconditional literal "://" emitted together with the scheme; it is never split into "scheme:" plus a conditional "//". Whenever scheme != "", "//" is emitted even if host is empty AND port is -1 AND path/query/fragment are all empty.

The scheme text emitted by to_string() is the stored, ASCII-lowercased scheme (lowercasing happens at construction, visible on line 1); no other scheme sanitization occurs — arbitrary characters (spaces, tabs, ':', '/') are passed through verbatim, so a scheme containing ':' or '//' produces doubled separators.

":" + port is appended immediately after host (inside the scheme gate) exactly when the stored port >= 0, i.e. exactly when port() != -1. Since the constructor normalizes any value outside [0,65535] to -1, the observable predicate "port >= 0", "port != -1" and "0 <= port <= 65535" are all equivalent; -1 is the only omitting value that port() can ever report. Port 0 IS included. The port is rendered as plain decimal of the normalized value (no zero padding, no sign).
The port block is independent of host emptiness: with scheme set and host empty, a valid port still produces "://" + "" + ":" + port.
Neither the authority nor to_string() is gated on is_valid(); invalid URLs still compose normally.

path is inserted verbatim from the stored path with NO separator logic: no '/' is inserted between authority and path, and no default "/" is substituted when path is empty. (The leading-slash fix-up happens at construction, not in to_string: a non-empty path not starting with '/' is stored as "/" + path, which path() on line 4 reveals.)

The "://" separator is emitted unconditionally after a non-empty scheme, even when host is empty and port<0 — producing "scheme://" with nothing after it (and "scheme:///path" when only path is set).
from_components does NOT re-split the PATH argument on '?' or '#'. Embedded '?'/'#' stay inside path(); query() and fragment() remain exactly as passed. This makes to_string() ambiguous/lossy.
A ':'+digits suffix embedded in HOST is NOT split into the port and does not override argv[3]; both appear, yielding a double colon-port in to_string().
"user:pass@" in HOST is NOT extracted as userinfo; the whole string is stored as host() verbatim and pasted before the ":port".
A full URL passed as the SCHEME argument is NOT parsed. It is only ASCII-lowercased and then has a literal "://" appended; host/path/query/fragment stay empty and is_valid()=0.

PATH normalization (the only structural mutation): if path is non-empty and path[0] != '/', a single '/' is prepended. Empty path stays empty. No other rewriting (no dot-segment collapsing, no '//' collapsing, no trimming, no percent re-coding).
SCHEME is ASCII-lowercased byte-wise, with no trimming, no validation, and no character filtering. HOST is never case-folded. Query/fragment never case-folded.

QUERY and FRAGMENT are stored byte-verbatim and prefixed with a literal '?' / '#' only when non-empty — a leading '?' in query or leading '#' in fragment is duplicated, and a '#' inside query is emitted raw.
is_valid() == (!host.empty() || !path.empty()) — evaluated after the path '/' -prepend. It is completely independent of scheme, port, query and fragment.

refutedRules.correctedRule: String LENGTH is irrelevant; only the numeric VALUE decides. out_of_range is thrown iff the mathematical value of [sign]DIGIT+ falls outside [-2147483648, 2147483647]. DIMENSION: host-transform — definitive spec after adversarial falsification (~870 invocations)

=== 0. PRECONDITIONS (not host-caused, but a Rust port must reproduce them) ===
if argc < 7 { exit(1) }                       // stdout AND stderr both empty. Verified for 0..5 args.
// argc > 7 is fine: args beyond the 6th are ignored. Verified with 7 and 9 args.
port_i32 = try_stoi(argv[3]) else { abort }   // C++ std::stoi. On failure ("", "abc", "--1", ".")
                                              // the process aborts with exit 134, stdout EMPTY (0 bytes),
                                              // stderr = "terminate called after throwing an instance of
                                              // 'std::invalid_argument'\n  what():  stoi\n".
                                              // NO host value can ever trigger this.
// stoi is prefix/whitespace tolerant: " 80"->80, "80x"->80, "+80"->80, "80 "->80, "0x50"->0, "1e3"->1.

=== 1. THE HOST TRANSFORM: IDENTITY ===
self.host: String = argv[2].to_owned();   // EXACTLY this. Nothing else.

Rust implementers: use the raw OsStr/Vec<u8> bytes. Do NOT do any of the following — every one of
them is PROVEN ABSENT by observation:
  - no ASCII or Unicode lowercasing / case folding  (host "EXAMPLE.COM" stays "EXAMPLE.COM" while
    scheme "HTTP" DOES become "http" in the same run)
  - no trim of leading/trailing/interior whitespace  (host "   " stays "   ")
  - no percent-encoding and no percent-decoding      ("%00" stays "%00"; "+" stays "+")
  - no IDNA / punycode in either direction           ("münchen.de" and "xn--mnchen-3ya.de" both verbatim)
  - no IPv6 bracket add or strip                     ("::1" stays bare, "[::1]" stays bracketed)
  - no dot normalization                             (".", "..", "example.com.", "a..b" all kept)
  - no ":port" split out of the host                 ("example.com:8080" stays whole)
  - no "user:pass@" userinfo split                   (kept inside host)
  - no "/", "?", "#" or "scheme://" extraction       (kept inside host)
  - no length limit, truncation, or rejection        (verbatim at every length 1..131000)
  - no character-class validation                    (no host value affects is_valid; see §4)
  - no locale sensitivity                            (11 locales incl. tr_TR/lt_LT identical)
Byte domain proven: every byte 0x01..=0xFF is passed through unchanged (exhaustive sweep, 255/255
byte-exact). 0x00 is unrepresentable in argv and therefore unobservable — a Rust String/&str is a
faithful model for every input the contract can actually deliver.

=== 2. OUTPUT LINE 2 ===
println!("{}", self.host);   // raw bytes, may itself contain '\n' (then it spans >1 physical line)

=== 3. HOST'S ROLE IN to_string() (LINE 7) ===
fn to_string(&self) -> String {
    let mut out = String::new();
    if !self.scheme.is_empty() {            // <-- SOLE gate on the whole authority. Not host, not port.
        out += &self.scheme;                //     scheme is the ALREADY-LOWERCASED value
        out += "://";                       //     emitted even when host is empty
        out += &self.host;                  //     raw, unescaped, unbracketed, unfolded
        if self.port >= 0 {                 //     0 counts; 0..=65535 retained, else stored as -1
            out += ":";
            out += &self.port.to_string();  //     NO default-port suppression: http:80, https:443 emitted
        }
    }
    // If scheme IS empty, host and port are BOTH silently discarded here even though host()/port()
    // still report them. Verified for port = -2147483648,-2,-1,0,1,80,443,8080,65535,65536,2147483647.
    out += &self.path;                      // path already normalized; host has NO influence on it
    if !self.query.is_empty()    { out += "?"; out += &self.query; }
    if !self.fragment.is_empty() { out += "#"; out += &self.fragment; }
    out
}

=== 4. HOST'S ROLE IN is_valid() (LINE 8) ===
fn is_valid(&self) -> bool { !self.host.is_empty() || !self.path.is_empty() }
Host contributes ONLY its emptiness — never its content, length, or character class. A single space,
a single "\n", a 131000-byte host, and "%00" all count as non-empty => true. scheme, port, query and
fragment are irrelevant. Proven by the exhaustive 64-case cross product
scheme{"", "s"} x host{"", "h"} x port{-1, 80} x path{"", "/p"} x query{"", "q"} x fragment{"", "f"}
=> 0 violations.

=== 5. CROSS-FIELD NON-INTERACTIONS (all proven, do not add coupling) ===
path_out = if argv[4].is_empty() { "" } else if starts_with('/') { argv[4] } else { "/" + argv[4] }
           // unconditional; NOT gated on host. host="" path="p" -> "/p".
Nothing about host changes scheme folding, port parsing/clamping, query, or fragment.
Nothing about those fields changes host.

refutedRules.correctedRule: For every path value tested (300+ runs, including 0xFF, 0x01, 0x7F, embedded LF/CR, bad escapes, 131000 bytes) the process exits 0 with empty stderr and prints exactly 8 logical fields. But path is only reached if the port argument parses: the program calls std::stoi(argv[3]) BEFORE constructing/printing anything, and a non-numeric or empty port arg raises an uncaught std::invalid_argument -> SIGABRT (wait status 134), no stdout at all. So: 'path content never causes nonzero exit or stderr; the only observed abnormal termination comes from the port argument and occurs before any path processing.'

NEW (resolves stated uncertainty #4): the length bound is at least 131,001 stored bytes, i.e. there is no program-imposed cap in the entire reachable range. path="/"+130999 'c' -> line4 length exactly 131000, first 8 and last 8 bytes correct, verbatim, line7 length 131011, line8=1, exit 0, no stderr. refutedRules.correctedRule: Empty scheme stays empty (no default is substituted). In to_string(), the scheme, the literal "://", the host, and the ":port" are ALL inside a single `if (scheme != "")` branch, so an empty scheme suppresses the whole `scheme://host:port` prefix and to_string() degrades to `normalized_path + ["?"+query] + ["#"+fragment]`. Emptiness is tested on the RAW/lowered scheme string (lowering can never create or destroy emptiness), and only the empty string triggers this -- any 1-byte scheme, including SPACE, TAB, LF, 0x01, 0x7F or 0xFF, is non-empty and keeps the full authority.

newRules: NEW: A scheme argv whose FIRST byte is NUL is delivered to the program as the empty string by execve, and is then indistinguishable from an explicitly empty scheme -- including the whole-authority collapse. ("\x00","example.com","80","/","","") -> stdout hex 0a6578616d706c652e636f6d0a38300a2f0a0a0a2f0a310a, i.e. line1 "", line7 "/", valid 1; ("\x00HTTP","example.com","80","/","","") -> byte-identical stdout; ("","example.com","80","/","","") control -> byte-identical stdout. (This is the argv layer, not the URL class -- interior NULs remain untestable via this CLI.)

NEW: The scheme VALUE has zero semantic effect anywhere. There is NO default-port suppression for any well-known scheme: ("http","example.com","80","/x","","") -> "http://example.com:80/x"; ("https","example.com","443","/x","","") -> "https://example.com:443/x"; ("ftp","example.com","21","/x","","") -> "ftp://example.com:21/x"; ("ws","example.com","80","/x","","") -> "ws://example.com:80/x". And no scheme-specific authority rules: ("file","","-1","/x","","") -> "file:///x", ("mailto","","-1","/x","","") -> "mailto:///x", ("urn","","-1","/x","","") -> "urn:///x" -- mailto/urn are treated exactly like http, emitting "://". A nonsense scheme behaves identically: ("ZZZ","example.com","443","/x","","") -> "zzz://example.com:443/x".

NEW: is_valid() never depends on the scheme -- not on its value and not on empty-vs-non-empty. DIMENSION: scheme-transform. Definitive spec after adversarial falsification (>4000 observed runs; 1 of 16 prior rules refuted as incomplete).

=== 1. THE TRANSFORM (applied to the raw scheme argv byte string) ===

    fn normalize_scheme(raw: &[u8]) -> Vec<u8> {
        raw.iter().map(|&b| if (0x41..=0x5A).contains(&b) { b + 0x20 } else { b }).collect()
    }

Properties, ALL observed, none inferred:
  * Pure, total, per-byte, stateless. Exactly bytes 0x41..0x5A map to 0x61..0x7A; the other 229
    testable bytes (0x01..0xFF) are identity. Both boundaries verified on both sides:
    0x40->0x40, 0x41->0x61, 0x5A->0x7A, 0x5B->0x5B, 0x60->0x60, 0x61->0x61, 0x7A->0x7A, 0x7B->0x7B.
  * Position-independent (verified at start, middle, end for all 255 bytes).
  * Length- and order-preserving; no dedup, insertion, or removal. len(out) == len(in) always.
  * Idempotent. Byte-identical to `LC_ALL=C tr 'A-Z' 'a-z'`.
  * NO trimming of leading/trailing whitespace (space, TAB, LF, CR, VT, FF, NBSP all preserved).
  * NO collapsing of internal whitespace.
  * NO stripping of control chars, including 0x09, 0x0A, 0x0B, 0x0C, 0x0D, 0x01, 0x1B, 0x7F.
  * NO stripping of a trailing ':', '/', '//' or '://'. NO separator dedup.
  * NO syntax validation, NO rejection, NO percent-decoding, NO percent-encoding.
  * Bytes >= 0x80 untouched: no UTF-8 case folding, no Latin-1 folding (0xDC stays 0xDC).
  * LOCALE-INDEPENDENT. Do NOT use a locale-sensitive to_lowercase / tolower.
    Rust: use `b.to_ascii_lowercase()` (or the range check above). Do NOT use `char::to_lowercase`
    or `str::to_lowercase` -- those would break on non-UTF-8 bytes and on Turkish/German data.
    Observed: LC_ALL in {C, POSIX, tr_TR, tr_TR.iso88599, de_DE.iso88591, en_US.utf8, de_DE.utf8,
    invalid_LOCALE, ""} all give the identical 26-byte map. 'I'(0x49)->'i'(0x69) even under tr_TR
    (NOT dotless), "SS"->"ss" (no eszett logic), 0xC4B0/0xC4B1 unchanged.
  * NO length cap and NO truncation. Verified exact at N = 0,1,2,63,64,65,127,128,129,255,256,257,
    1023,1024,4095,4096,65535,65536,100000,131000,131071. N=131072 is refused by the OS at execve
    (E2BIG, rc=127, no stdout) -- an argv limit, not a program limit. Treat as unbounded.
  * Empty in -> empty out. The transform can never create or destroy emptiness.

=== 2. STORAGE / ACCESSOR ===

Store the normalized bytes. scheme() (stdout line 1) prints exactly those bytes.
to_string() (line 7) reuses the SAME normalized bytes, so line7 always begins with line1 + "://"
for any non-empty scheme. Whether lowering happens once at construction or in each accessor is
UNOBSERVABLE in a black box (the map is idempotent) -- implement it once at construction.

=== 3. to_string() COMPOSITION -- the load-bearing part, with the refuted rule corrected ===

    fn to_string(&self) -> String {
        let mut s = String::new();
        if !self.scheme.is_empty() {              // <-- host AND port live INSIDE this branch
            s += &self.scheme;                    // already lowercased
            s += "://";                           // exactly these 3 bytes, unconditionally
            s += &self.host;                      // verbatim, NEVER case-changed
            if self.port >= 0 { s += &format!(":{}", self.port); }   // port 0 IS emitted
        }
        s += &self.path;                          // path already normalized (see sec. 5)
        if !self.query.is_empty()    { s += "?"; s += &self.query; }
        if !self.fragment.is_empty() { s += "#"; s += &self.fragment; }
        s
    }

CRITICAL, and where the previous investigator was wrong: when scheme == "" the host and the port
are dropped TOO, not merely the scheme and "://".
    ("", "EXAMPLE.COM", "8080", "/PATH", "Q=1", "FRAG") -> line7 == "/PATH?Q=1#FRAG"
    (NOT "EXAMPLE.COM:8080/PATH?Q=1#FRAG")
    ("", "example.com", "0",  "/p", "q", "f")           -> line7 == "/p?q#f"
    ("", "example.com", "80", "",   "q", "" )           -> line7 == "?q"
    ("", "e",           "-1", "",   "",  "" )           -> line7 == ""      and is_valid == 1
Any non-empty scheme, even a single space, keeps the authority:
    (" ", "EXAMPLE.COM", "8080", "/PATH", "Q=1", "FRAG") -> " ://EXAMPLE.COM:8080/PATH?Q=1#FRAG"

=== 5. INTERACTIONS THIS DIMENSION DOES NOT OWN BUT MUST RESPECT ===

  * Case is changed for the scheme ONLY. host/path/query/fragment are byte-verbatim, in every
    config including scheme=="" ("EXAMPLE.COM" stays uppercase; "EX%41MPLE.COM" stays as-is).
  * Path is normalized BEFORE to_string composes it: non-empty path not starting with '/' gets a
    leading '/' prepended ("P" -> "/P"). to_string uses the normalized path.
  * port < 0 omits ":port"; port == 0 emits ":0". Both only when scheme is non-empty.
  * is_valid() is COMPLETELY independent of the scheme (value and emptiness). Consistent with
    is_valid == (host != "" || normalized_path != ""); verified over 6 configs x 16 schemes,

  * (CLOSED) 0x0A is now covered mechanically, not by eyeball, via whole-stdout byte comparison.

refutedRules.originalRule: IDEMPOTENCE / round-trip: the component normalization is a fixed point. Re-feeding the printed components (lines 1-6) as the 6 args ALWAYS reproduces byte-identical 8-line output.
refutedRules.counterexample: The word "always" is false because the printed-lines-to-args mapping is not well-defined when a field contains a newline. ("http", $'a\nb', "80", "/p", "", "") emits TEN lines [http|a|b|80|/p|||http://a|b:80/p|1], so stdout lines 1-6 are ("http","a","b","80","/p",""). Re-feeding those six lines makes argv[3]="b", which hits stoi: exit=134, stderr "terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::invalid_argument' / what(): stoi", stdout EMPTY. So the observed round-trip goes from a valid 10-line output to an abort, not to byte-identical output.
refutedRules.correctedRule: The component normalization IS a true fixed point when you re-feed the actual component VALUES: normalize(normalize(x)) == normalize(x) for all six fields (verified over 20160 grid cases, nonidempotent=0; re-running ("http",$'a\nb',"80","/p","","") with the same value arguments reproduces byte-identical output). What is NOT round-trippable is the line-oriented stdout FORMAT: if any of scheme/host/path/query/fragment contains 0x0A, stdout has more than 8 lines and lines 1-6 no longer correspond to the components, so a line-based re-feed harness is invalid (and typically aborts via stoi). Implementers must not treat the 8-line stdout as a parseable serialization.

refutedRules.originalRule: PORT: value = std::stoi(argv[3]) (leading whitespace/sign allowed, stops at first non-digit).
refutedRules.counterexample: "leading whitespace/sign allowed" is too loose: it wrongly predicts success for repeated or whitespace-separated signs. ("http","h","++80","/","","") -> exit=134, std::invalid_argument (not 80). ("http","h","--80","/","","") -> exit=134, std::invalid_argument (not 80, and not -80). ("http","h","+ 80","/","","") and ("http","h","- 80","/","","") -> exit=134 std::invalid_argument.
refutedRules.correctedRule: The accepted grammar is exactly strtol base-10 prefix syntax: [isspace()*][ '+' | '-' ]digit+ , i.e. any run of whitespace (space, \t, \n, \v, \f, \r) then AT MOST ONE sign then AT LEAST ONE ASCII digit 0-9; parsing stops at the first byte that is not an ASCII digit and the remainder is ignored without error. Whitespace may only precede the sign, never follow it. Confirmed: " 80"->80, "  80"->80, "\t80"->80, "\n80"->80, "+80"->80, "+0"->0, "-0"->0, "-00"->0, "007"->7, "0080"->80, "80 "->80, "80abc"->80, "80.5"->80, "65535."->65535, "1_000"->1, "0x50"->0, "0X50"->0, "0b11"->0, "1e3"->1, " +65535 "->65535, " -1"->-1, "-1 "->-1. Only ASCII digits count: "٣" and "２" throw invalid_argument. "-2147483648" parses (then clamps to -1) but "-2147483649" throws out_of_range, pinning the target type as 32-bit int.

refutedRules.originalRule: Fields are passed through byte-exactly with no length limit and no escaping.
refutedRules.counterexample: "no length limit" fails at the process-creation boundary. host=path=900000 'z' bytes: the binary never runs — execve returns E2BIG ("Argument list too long"), exit status 126 from the shell, 0 stdout lines. This is a real, reachable failure mode for a caller passing very large components.
refutedRules.correctedRule: The BINARY imposes no length limit and never truncates: 5000 bytes/field gives line1=5000, line2=5000, line4=5001 (leading '/'), line5=5000, line6=5000, line7=25009, line8=1; 100000 bytes/field gives line7=400013 bytes, exit 0, valid=1 — both exactly matching the concatenation formula. The limit is external (execve ARG_MAX): at ~900000 bytes x 2 fields the exec itself fails with E2BIG before any of the program's code runs, so there is no output and no exit code from the program. A Rust reimplementation should replicate the unlimited in-process behavior and need not reproduce the E2BIG boundary, which belongs to the OS.

newRules: NEW (cross-field, high value): to_string()-emptiness and is_valid() are COMPLETELY DECOUPLED in both directions. (a) Valid but stringifies to EMPTY: ("","hh","-1","","","") -> line7="" (empty), line8=1. Same for ("","hh","80","","","") and ("","hh","65535","","","") -> line7="", line8=1. --- 0. PROGRAM ENTRY / ORDERING (strict three stages) ---
main(argc, argv):

  if argc - 1 < 6:                      # fewer than 6 positional args
      exit(1)                           # stdout: 0 bytes. stderr: 0 bytes. No message anywhere.

  scheme_in   = argv[1]; host_in = argv[2]; port_in = argv[3]
  path_in     = argv[4]; query_in = argv[5]; frag_in = argv[6]
  # All are NUL-free byte strings (execve guarantees; NUL is unreachable).

  # STAGE 2 — port parse. May terminate the process. Nothing has been
  # printed or normalized yet, so stdout is guaranteed EMPTY on failure.
  port = parse_port(port_in)             # see section 1

  # STAGE 3 — normalize + print. Cannot fail.

--- 1. parse_port(s) -> i32 ---
# Grammar is exactly strtol/stoi base-10 PREFIX syntax:
#   [ WS* ] [ '+' | '-' ] DIGIT+        WS = {' ','\t','\n','\v','\f','\r'}

# At most ONE sign, and whitespace may precede the sign but NEVER follow it.
# Parsing stops at the first non-digit; the remainder is discarded silently.
fn parse_port(s):
    (v, ok, overflow) = strtol_i32_prefix(s)
    if not ok:        ABORT_INVALID_ARGUMENT()   # no digits found after optional WS+sign
    if overflow:      ABORT_OUT_OF_RANGE()       # value outside i32 range
    if v < 0 or v > 65535: return -1             # CLAMP to the sentinel
    return v

#                   "e5" "++80" "--80" "+ 80" "- 80" "٣" "２"
# out_of_range:     "2147483648" "99999999999999999999" "-2147483649"
# NOTE: EMPTY port string ABORTS. There is no default port.
# NOTE: the clamp is observationally identical whether written as
#   (v<0||v>65535) or as an unsigned range test; either is correct.

--- 2. ascii_lower(s) — applies to SCHEME ONLY ---
for each byte b: if 0x41 <= b <= 0x5A { b += 0x20 }   # else unchanged
# EXHAUSTIVE: bytes 1..255 scanned; ONLY 0x41..0x5A change. No trimming,
# no validation, no filtering, no length rule, no non-ASCII case folding.
# LOCALE-INDEPENDENT (C, C.UTF-8, en_US.UTF-8, tr_TR.UTF-8,
# en_US.ISO-8859-1, POSIX, invalid all identical). Use ASCII arithmetic,
# NOT a locale-aware tolower.
#   "HTTP"->"http"  " HTTP "->" http "  "HTTP:"->"http:"
#   "HTTP://"->"http://"  "1HTTP"->"1http"  "A-B_C+D.E~F"->"a-b_c+d.e~f"
#   "ÄÖÜI"->"ÄÖÜi" (bytes c3 84 c3 96 c3 9c 69)
# HOST, QUERY, FRAGMENT are NEVER case-folded (254-byte scans: 0 changes).

--- 3. normalize_path(p) ---
if p.is_empty():        return ""             # empty stays empty
if p.as_bytes()[0] == 0x2F ('/'): return p    # unchanged
return "/" + p                                # prepend exactly one '/'
# EXHAUSTIVE over all 254 testable first bytes. This is the ONLY structural
# mutation in the whole program. NO dot-segment collapsing, NO '//'
# collapsing, NO trimming, NO percent re-coding, NO backslash conversion.
# Independent of scheme/host/port/query/fragment.
#  "a"->"/a"  " "->"/ "  "\t"->"/\t"  "\\a"->"/\\a"  "."->"/."  ".."->"/.."
#  "?"->"/?"  "#"->"/#"  "?#"->"/?#"  "?q"->"/?q"  "%2F"->"/%2F"
#  "./a/../b"->"/./a/../b"   "a/../../../../etc/passwd" -> "/a/../../../../etc/passwd"
#  "/"->"/"  "//"->"//"  "///"->"///"  "//evil.com/x"->"//evil.com/x"

--- 4. to_string() — PURE CONCATENATION, NO RE-PARSING ---
fn to_string(scheme, host, port, path, query, frag) -> String:
    s = ""
    if !scheme.is_empty():               # <-- the ONLY gate on the authority
        s += scheme
        s += "://"                       # UNCONDITIONAL after a non-empty scheme
        s += host                        # even if empty
        if port >= 0:                    # 0 IS emitted; -1 is not
            s += ":" + itoa(port)
    s += path                            # normalized path
    if !query.is_empty(): s += "?" + query
    if !frag.is_empty():  s += "#" + frag
    return s

# CROSS-FIELD LAWS (each independently verified):
# L1. scheme.is_empty() erases the ENTIRE authority — host AND ":"+port —
#     even though host() and port() still report them.
#       ("","hh","80","","","")     -> line2="hh" line3="80" line7=""   (EMPTY!)
#       ("","hh","65535","","","")  -> line7=""
#       ("","","80","/p","","")     -> line7="/p"
#       ("","","0","/p","q","f")    -> line7="/p?q#f"
#       ("","hh","-1","//evil.com/x","","") -> line7="//evil.com/x"
# L2. A non-empty scheme ALWAYS yields "://", even with empty host and port<0.
#       ("http","","-1","","","")    -> line7="http://"        line8=0
#       ("http","","-1","/p","","")  -> line7="http:///p"      line8=1
#       ("http","","-1","","","f")   -> line7="http://#f"      line8=0
#       ("http","","-1","","q","")   -> line7="http://?q"      line8=0
#       ("file","","-1","/etc/hosts","","") -> line7="file:///etc/hosts"
#     Any non-empty scheme qualifies, however absurd:
#       (" ","hh","80","/p","","")   -> line7=" ://hh:80/p"
#       (":","hh","80","/p","","")   -> line7=":://hh:80/p"
#       ("//","hh","80","/p","","")  -> line7="//://hh:80/p"
#       ("http://h:80/p?q#f","","-1","","","") -> line7="http://h:80/p?q#f://"
# L3. ":"+port is emitted with an EMPTY host, giving a bare-colon authority:
#       ("http","","80","","","")    -> line7="http://:80"     line8=0
#       ("http","","0","","","")     -> line7="http://:0"      line8=0
#       ("http","","0","/p","","")   -> line7="http://:0/p"    line8=1
#       ("http","","80","a","","")   -> line4="/a" line7="http://:80/a"
# L4. HOST is an opaque byte string. ':'+digits, userinfo, '/', '?', '#'
#     are NEVER split out and NEVER override argv[3]:
#       ("http","h:9090","80","/","","")  -> line7="http://h:9090:80/"
#       (":80","8080")                    -> line7="http://:80:8080/"
#       ("h:","80")                       -> line7="http://h::80/"
#       ("h:99999","80")                  -> line7="http://h:99999:80/"
#       ("[::1]","8080")                  -> line7="http://[::1]:8080/"
#       ("u:p@h","80")                    -> line7="http://u:p@h:80/"
#       ("@","80")->"http://@:80/"  ("u@",-1)->"http://u@"  ("@h",-1)->"http://@h"
#       ("h/x","80","/y")                 -> line7="http://h/x:80/y"
#       ("h?q","80","/y","z")             -> line7="http://h?q:80/y?z"
#       ("h#f","80","/y","","g")          -> line7="http://h#f:80/y#g"
#       ("h//x","80","")                  -> line7="http://h//x:80"
# L5. PATH is never re-split on '?' or '#' (true whether or not query/frag
#     are set), so to_string() is ambiguous:
#       ("http","h","80","/p?x=1#f","","") -> 4="/p?x=1#f" 5="" 6=""
#                                            7="http://h:80/p?x=1#f"
#       ("http","h","80","/a?b#c","d?e#f","g?h#i")
#            -> 7="http://h:80/a?b#c?d?e#f#g?h#i"
# L6. '?'/'#' prefixes depend ONLY on the emptiness of their own field and
#     are never de-duplicated; whitespace counts as non-empty:
#       ("http","h","80","/","?q","")   -> 7="http://h:80/??q"
#       ("http","h","80","/","","?x")   -> 7="http://h:80/#?x"
#       ("http","h","80","/","?","#")   -> 7="http://h:80/??##"
#       ("http","h","80","/","#","")    -> 7="http://h:80/?#"
#       ("http","h","80","/"," "," ")   -> 7="http://h:80/? # "
#       ("http","h","80","","q","f")    -> 7="http://h:80?q#f"   (no path!)
#       ("http","h","-1","","q","")     -> 7="http://h?q"
#       ("","","-1","","q","")          -> 7="?q"
#       ("","","-1","","","f")          -> 7="#f"
#       ("","","-1","","q","f")         -> 7="?q#f"
# L7. NO percent-encoding/decoding/escaping ever:
#       ("http","h","80","/%2Fa%20b","k=%26v","%23f")
#            -> 7="http://h:80/%2Fa%20b?k=%26v#%23f"
#       ("ht%74p","%68","80","/%00","%","%%") -> 7="ht%74p://%68:80/%00?%#%%"
#       ("http","a b","80","/a b","a b","a b") -> 7="http://a b:80/a b?a b#a b"

--- 5. is_valid() ---
fn is_valid(host, path) -> bool:  return !host.is_empty() || !path.is_empty()
# Independent of scheme, port, query and fragment. 384-combo truth table
# (scheme{"",http,file," "} x host{"","h"," "} x path{"","/p","p"," "} x
#  port{-1,0,80,70000} x (query,frag){("",""),("q","f")}) -> 0 mismatches.
# Because normalize_path never empties a non-empty path nor fills an empty
# one, testing raw vs normalized path is observationally identical.
#   ("http","","0","","","")    -> 0   (though line7="http://:0")
#   ("http","","80","","q","f") -> 0   (though line7="http://:80?q#f")
#   ("http","h","70000","","","") -> line3="-1", line8=1 (bad port never invalidates)
#   (""," ","-1","","","")      -> 1   (a single-space host is "valid")
#   ("","","-1"," ","","")      -> 1   (path becomes "/ ")
# DECOUPLING (do NOT conflate with to_string emptiness):
#   valid + empty string:   ("","hh","-1","","","")  -> 7=""        8=1
#   invalid + non-empty:    ("http","","0","","","") -> 7="http://:0" 8=0
#   to_string()=="" exactly when scheme,path,query,frag are ALL empty;
#   in that case validity == !host.is_empty().

--- 6. NON-INJECTIVITY (to_string cannot be reversed) ---
# Distinct component tuples with IDENTICAL line 7:
#   ("http","h","80","/p?x=1#f","","")  ==  ("http","h","80","/p","x=1","f")
#        both -> "http://h:80/p?x=1#f"
#   ("http","h:9090","-1","/x","","")   ==  ("http","h","9090","/x","","")
#        both -> "http://h:9090/x"
#   ("http","/p","-1","","","")         ==  ("http","","-1","/p","","")
#        both -> "http:///p"            (host/path swap collides)
#   ("http","h","-1","/x?y","","")      ==  ("http","h","-1","/x","y","")
#        both -> "http://h/x?y"
# STRONGEST CASE — same string, DIFFERENT validity:
#   ("","hh","-1","","","") -> 7="" 8=1   vs   ("","","-1","","","") -> 7="" 8=0
# There is no from_string()/parse() entry point on this CLI; all 6 args are
# components. Never attempt to recover components from line 7.

--- 7. IDEMPOTENCE ---
# normalize is a true fixed point on VALUES: re-feeding the six component
# values reproduces byte-identical output (20,160/20,160 cases).
# ascii_lower, the '/'-prepend and the port clamp are each idempotent;
# junk ports converge in one pass ("80abc"->80->80; "70000"->-1->-1).
# CAVEAT: the 8-line stdout is NOT a parseable serialization. If any of
# scheme/host/path/query/fragment contains 0x0A, stdout has MORE than 8
# lines and lines 1-6 no longer equal the components:
#   ("http", "a\nb", "80", "/p", "", "") -> 10 lines:
#     http | a | b | 80 | /p |  |  | http://a | b:80/p | 1
#   Re-feeding those lines makes argv[3]="b" -> exit 134 std::invalid_argument.
# CR (0x0D) is retained without shifting lines: host="a\rb" ->
#   line2="a\rb", line7="http://a\rb:80/".
# A newline inside PORT never shifts lines (port becomes an int).
